# Tako

> Tako is a data intelligence platform. The Tako MCP server gives AI agents premium live data from authoritative providers and web search in one call. Agents can also discover what data Tako holds, fetch the rows or page text behind a result, explore the data graph, and opt in to chart creation or Tako's Answer Agent and Company Agent. It is a hosted remote MCP server on Cloudflare Workers.

## Documentation

- [MCP Server Setup](https://github.com/TakoData/tako-mcp): Connect to the hosted Tako MCP server
- [API Reference](https://tako.com/docs/): Full REST API documentation
- [Chart Gallery](https://tako.com/gallery): Browse example charts and visualizations
- [OpenAPI Spec](https://tako.com/openapi.yaml): Machine-readable API specification

## Connecting

Hosted endpoint: `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). The ChatGPT app uses its own OAuth-only surface at `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp/chatgpt`.

- No token needed: paste the URL and sign in when the client prompts — a per-host key is minted automatically, and a new account gets up to 2,000 free requests. Anonymous connections work immediately: `tako_search` runs (rate-limited, shared capacity); every other tool stays listed and answers with sign-in instructions when called.
- CI, headless runs, and clients without an OAuth flow: pass `Authorization: Bearer <TAKO_API_KEY>` on the same URL. Get a key at tako.com/console/api-keys.

Choosing tools: `?tools=` on the endpoint URL is an ALLOWLIST that REPLACES the default listing, so name every tool you want in one comma-separated list. Tokens are tool names with the `tako_` prefix optional, e.g. `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp?tools=search,available_data,contents,agent`. Listed by default: `tako_search`, `tako_available_data`, `tako_contents`, `tako_graph_related`. Opt-in, so reachable only by naming them: `tako_search_advanced` (the whole v3 search body, plus `include_answer` for one synthesized, citation-backed answer and `output_schema` for structured output), `tako_agent` (the multi-step Answer Agent; listed by default on `/mcp/chatgpt`), `tako_company_agent` (the multi-step Company Agent, for which companies or people match registry facts; name `company_agent`; listed by default on `/mcp/chatgpt`), `tako_visualize` (listed by default on `/mcp/chatgpt`, the surface whose host renders its chart widget inline). Unknown tokens are ignored, and a param that names nothing recognizable serves the defaults, so a typo never breaks the connection. `/mcp/chatgpt` ignores the param: its listing is fixed.

Pinning sources: `?sources=` on the `/mcp` URL pins the sources for the whole connection, for evaluating Tako data on its own. `?sources=data` searches Tako data only, `?sources=web` searches the web only, and `?sources=data,web` always searches both, e.g. `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp?sources=data`. It applies to `tako_search`, `tako_search_advanced`, `tako_agent`, and `tako_company_agent`: the `sources` input (on `tako_search_advanced`, the other source's block) leaves the tool's schema, and every call sends the pinned value, agent thread follow-ups included. `tako_contents`, `tako_available_data`, and `tako_graph_related` take no `sources` input; for web only, you can also drop the graph tools with `?tools=`, e.g. `?tools=search&sources=web`. An invalid or empty value fails the connection with an HTTP 400 that names the parameter; other unknown parameters are ignored. The server instructions state the pin when it applies. `/mcp/chatgpt` ignores the param.

Tools are discovered at runtime via `tools/list`. There is no per-call `api_token` argument — auth is connection-level.

## Available Tools

### Getting values vs. getting pointers

Two tools, one step apart — `tako_search` locates, `tako_contents` reads:

- **Recon and fan-outs**: `tako_search`. Cards carry headline values, node ids, and chart links. Cheap; fire many narrow one-entity+one-metric queries in parallel and assemble the result yourself. Every card renders as a chart on the ChatGPT app and for a `/mcp` client that declares MCP Apps support; any other `/mcp` client gets the first card's chart as an image.
- **The values themselves**: `tako_contents` on an `exportable: true` card's url — the card's rows, up to 2,000 inline. To analyze rows in code, set `delivery: "link"` and download the CSV before the link expires. `/mcp/chatgpt` returns rows inline only.
- **A web page's text**: `tako_contents` on the web result's url.

Never send a broad or multi-part question as one call — split it into narrow entity+metric searches (e.g. "US CPI inflation", "US core CPI inflation", "US PCE inflation", "US core PCE inflation"). When the user asks for Tako's agent or for multi-step research with Tako, use `tako_agent` (opt-in).

### tako_search
Reconnaissance and chart retrieval across Tako's data graph and the live web, returned as structured `cards` plus `web_results`; every card renders as a chart on the ChatGPT app and for a `/mcp` client that declares MCP Apps support (a carousel of interactive charts in one widget for two or more); any other `/mcp` client gets the first card's chart as an image. It locates data; `tako_contents` reads it. Cards carry headline values, node ids and chart links — right for breadth (many narrow queries fanned out in parallel to see what exists), for a chart when the embed is the deliverable, and to harvest node ids and urls.

Built to fan out: each query should resolve one metric — for one entity, or a comparison set ("Apple revenue", "Nvidia vs AMD gross margin") — and many narrow queries fired in parallel retrieve far better than one query carrying several metrics or topics. To see what proprietary data exists, ask `tako_available_data`; it returns each metric's EXACT canonical name. For a card's rows call `tako_contents` — only when the card is marked `exportable: true`. A non-exportable card (`exportable: false`, usually license-gated) carries no rows on any path: read its headline value from the card's `description` when it carries one. Repeated source/methodology paragraphs are hoisted out of the cards into the trailing Source notes section, and metric definitions into Definitions — both keyed by a card's `source` field verbatim, so look that string up there (truncating clients lose boilerplate before data). For open-ended research use `tako_agent` (opt-in). Results arrive as a markdown document, in this order: a `>` guidance line when a keyless search returns a placeholder card, `## Data cards` (per card: headline, exportable flag, node ids, url), a `Top card chart —` line carrying the embed and image urls, `## Web results`, `## Definitions`, `## Source notes`, and a usage footer. On `tako_search_advanced`, the `>` guidance line instead marks a `strict: true` pin that returned no cards, and `include_answer` puts the answer first, above everything else, the guidance line included, and adds `## Structured output` (or a `>` line naming why it is absent) and `## Related queries`; this tool emits none of those three. This tool never inlines rows — a card's rows are a `tako_contents` call on its url, and only when it is `exportable: true`. The markdown is COMPLETE, not an index: every field the structured payload carries — web-result snippets included — renders there too, because many hosts feed the model only that channel.

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): Natural-language query — one metric, on one entity or a comparison set; parallelize multiple. Wrap a multi-word name in double quotes to keep it one entity (`"tesla motors" club revenue`), and append `:LABEL` to force its type (`"Tesla":PRODUCT price`; PERSON, ORG, GPE, LOC, PRODUCT, DATE, EVENT, MONEY, CARDINAL, METRIC, TIME_PERIOD, UNITS). Tako strips the quotes before it searches. An unpaired quote disables quoting for the whole query — silently, so check both marks — a quoted phrase caps at 80 characters, and an unknown label stays in the query text. To find a person, search the name alone (`Jane Doe`); extra words drop the list. A list of people or companies is one query (`CFOs in Austin`, `fintechs in London`); its card's `description` doesn't name the matches, so call `tako_contents` on the card's url for the rows.
- `sources` (array): both by default (`["data","web"]`). Keep both unless the user asks for one.
- `country_code` (string, optional): ISO country code. Omit it for the server default, US.
- `locale` (string, optional): Locale. Omit it for the server default, en-US.

Four parameters, and it declares no defaults of its own: an omitted field is omitted from the request, so the server's default applies. The one exception is `highlights` on the web source, always on, so each snippet carries the query-relevant passages rather than the page's opening characters. For a per-source result count, inline rows, a graph pin, a web domain filter, or `effort: deep`, use `tako_search_advanced` (opt-in, `?tools=search_advanced`).

### tako_search_advanced
Opt-in tool — off by default; enable with `?tools=search_advanced` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). It exposes the v3 `POST /api/v3/search` body WHOLE: every field of the request and of both source blocks, derived from the published schema. The top level and both source blocks are strict, so a field the API does not have is an error rather than a silent drop. Use `tako_search` unless you need an option it does not carry: a per-source result count, inline card rows, a graph pin, a web domain or category filter, or the `deep` effort tier. Nothing is sent unless you set it, with two exceptions — web `highlights` and `variable_cost` default to true here, and `web: {"highlights": false}` or `variable_cost: false` turns each off. Naming a source block — even as an empty object — is what selects that source; omit both and the server searches data and web. The structured payload is `tako_search`'s plus the four root fields only this tool can produce — `answer`, `structured_output`, `structured_output_error` and `related`; `tako_search` declares none of them, because it cannot reach the answer endpoint. It also carries `cards[].rows`, the inlined rows `data.include_contents` asks for, which `tako_search` cannot request and does not declare. The other difference is that this tool does not auto-render the top card as an inline chart, so read `embed_url` for the chart. This is also the values channel for non-exportable cards: when a search card is `exportable: false` (usually license-gated), re-ask here with that card's METRIC node id ALONE (the `mt::` entry in its `nodes`) in `data.node_ids`, `strict: true`, and `data.include_contents: true` — pinning every node id on the card re-admits its other cards, and omitting `strict` only boosts, which measured as not enough to land the metric.

Parameters:
- `query` (string, required): Natural-language query — one metric per query retrieves best, the same as on the simple tool, and the same quoting syntax applies.
- `effort` (string, "fast" | "instant" | "deep", optional): Omit for the server default (fast). "instant" serves cached embeds without a new retrieval; "deep" widens retrieval and adds an LLM rerank — slower, and billed at a premium tier.
- `country_code` (string, optional): ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Omit for the server default, US.
- `locale` (string, optional): BCP-47 tag. Omit for the server default, en-US.
- `location` (object, optional): `{latitude, longitude}` of the end user, for implicit-location queries such as weather. An explicit location in the query wins.
- `timezone` (string, optional): IANA timezone (for example `America/New_York`). It localizes dates in rendered card images only — it does not shift how a relative date in the query is read.
- `output_settings` (object, optional): `image_dark_mode` for card preview images; `force_refresh` is informational on these endpoints.
- `include_related` (integer 1-20, optional): Return up to N follow-up query suggestions in `related`. Omit to disable. Search path only: `POST /api/v1/answer` accepts the field and returns no `related`, so it does nothing under `include_answer: true`.
- `variable_cost` (boolean, optional): Return website-traffic and SEO data (Semrush). Each such card bills the source's per-unit minimum above the request price. Defaults to true here; set false to get those cards as placeholders with no data points.
- `include_answer` (boolean, optional): Set true to run the answer endpoint (`POST /api/v1/answer`) instead of search — one synthesized, citation-backed answer in `answer`, with the retrieved cards and web results as its citations. Every other option applies the same way except `include_related`, which the answer endpoint ignores.
- `output_schema` (object, optional): JSON Schema to fill from the same evidence as the answer, returned in `structured_output`. Requires `include_answer: true`; sending it without that is rejected before any request goes out.
- `data` (object, optional): Tako data source settings — `count` (1-20; server default 5), `include_contents` (server default false), `max_rows` (omit for your account's inline cap, up to the 2,000-row ceiling), `content_format` (`json_compact` | `json_records` | `csv` | `card_json`), `node_ids` (up to 20 graph node ids to pin), `strict` (hard filter over the pinned nodes), `mode` (a documented no-op for Tako cards). To land on exactly one metric, pin THAT metric's node id alone with `strict: true` and name the entity in the query text; adding the entity's own id widens the filter back out. If that call returns 0 cards, drop `node_ids` and run the query text alone — the graph holds near-duplicate metric nodes where only one twin carries cards.
- `web` (object, optional): Web source settings — `count` (1-20; server default 5), `include_contents` (page text; server default false), `include_domains` / `exclude_domains` (bare hosts, max 20 each), `category` (`news` | `sports` | `finance`), `snippet_max_chars` (server default 4000), `highlights` (query-relevant passages instead of the page opening; this tool defaults it to true — set false for the page opening), `published_after` / `published_before` (ISO dates bounding the page's publish date), `article_content_max_chars` (cap on the inlined page text `include_contents` returns; server default 30000).

### tako_contents
Fetch the full content behind a url: a web page's extracted text, or an exportable Tako card's data rows. It's the step after search when you need the whole payload to compute over or quote. Batch up to 10 urls in one call — one call for 8 urls saves 7 round trips, and every extra round trip re-sends the whole conversation as input tokens.

Precondition (Tako cards): a card marked `exportable: false` is usually license-gated and returns no rows on any path, so read its headline value from the card's `description` instead. Call only on `exportable: true` cards, and even then a rare card still 403s, because the export gate is stricter than the flag — read the headline rather than retrying. Web urls always work.

Results ride in `results`, positionally aligned with the urls you passed, failures included. Each entry carries `url` and `cost`, plus exactly one of `rows` (a card's data as `{columns, rows, total_rows}`, with positional cells and `null` for a missing value), `text` (a web page), or `error`. `truncated` reports a cut payload, and `note` says whether `text` holds the passages for `query` or the whole page. Root `usage.total_cost_usd` is the call's total.

With `delivery: "link"`, a card's entry carries `download` (`url`, `expires_at`, `file_format`, `total_rows`) instead of inline data. With `format: "card"`, it carries `card`, the card's own structure. To analyze rows in code, use `delivery: "link"` and download the file right away. A premium cell comes back as `null` inline and as `[premium: withheld]` in a CSV link, and `note` names its column. `/mcp/chatgpt` takes no `delivery` or `format` and returns rows inline only.

Parameters:
- `urls` (array of string, 1-10, required): The result urls to fetch — a Tako card's `url`, web-result urls, or a mix. Each is fetched independently, and one url failing doesn't fail the others (its entry carries an `error` instead of a payload).
- `max_rows` (integer, 1-100,000, optional): Tako cards only — how many rows to return. Omit it for up to 2,000 rows. Charges scale with rows returned, so lower it when the recent rows are enough. Above 2,000 needs `delivery: "link"`. Ignored for web urls (use `max_chars`).
- `delivery` (`inline` or `link`, optional): Tako cards only. `inline` returns the data in the result. `link` returns a download link that expires 5 minutes after the call: a CSV file, or a JSON file with `format: "card"`. Use `link` when you can run shell commands and want to analyze the data in code. Ignored for web urls.
- `format` (`rows` or `card`, optional): Tako cards only. `rows` returns the card's data as one table. `card` returns the card's own structure, such as a company card's tabs. A card type without its own structure returns `rows`. Ignored for web urls.
- `offset` (integer, 0-100,000, optional): Tako list cards only — rows to skip, in the card's own order. With `max_rows`, it fetches one slice of a long list, such as the one row a person is on. The row order can change between calls, so check the name on each row you get. A card with a date column refuses it.
- `premium` (boolean, optional): Tako cards only — `true` returns a card's premium cells. A `tako_search` card shows each one as 🔒. Charges scale with the rows that hold one, so set it only when the user asks, and only for the rows they want. If a row has its own Tako link, in its cells or in the card's `description`, pass that link with `max_rows: 1` to get only that row. Otherwise set `offset` and `max_rows` to those rows. Not with `format: "card"`.
- `max_chars` (integer, 1-1,000,000, optional): Web urls only — character cap on the extracted page text. A single fetch defaults to 100,000; a batch splits a 250,000-character total evenly across its urls. `truncated: true` reports a cut. With `query`, it caps the passages instead: 100 to 20,000 characters, and 4,000 by default. Ignored for Tako card urls.
- `query` (string, optional): Web urls only — a question the passages should answer. The result holds the passages of the page that answer it instead of the whole page, so one call lands on the relevant section of a long document. A ' … ' marks a break between passages, so never quote across it as one sentence. Omit it to get the whole page. A `query` with no letter or digit counts as omitted. Ignored for Tako urls. If Tako can't get passages from a page, the result holds the whole page, and `note` says so.

### tako_available_data
Find what proprietary, continuously-updated structured data exists on something — summarized in one call. Ask it when the question IS coverage: what does Tako have on X, is this measure tracked at all, what is it called. Search on the canonical name it returns. Works on an entity (a company, person, or place → the metrics tracked on it, e.g. Tesla) or a metric (→ the entities it is tracked across, e.g. Inflation Rate), reported as a natural-language summary you can show the user.

Two paths, chosen by whether you pass `metric`:
- **Lookup** (`q` + `metric`, e.g. `q="Carnival", metric="passenger cruise days"`) — resolves the entity+metric PAIR directly in ~0.6s and returns a runnable `next_call`. Use it whenever you already know the measure.
- **Discovery** (`q` alone) — lists what the resolved node covers, for browsing. Candidate names are relevance-gated against `q` (name matches rank above alias matches), so a fuzzy graph hit about a different company is not reported as coverage.
- **Both kinds** — when `q` alone names an entity and a metric ("US core PCE" → the company Core and the metric Core PCE Price Index), the tool returns both as candidates (subtype, label, aliases, coverage count) and renders neither. Re-run with `types` or `metric`.
- **Browse filter** — `metric` is sent as the API's substring filter on the entity's metrics, so `q="Nvidia", metric="data center"` returns every matching metric with its node id, not a 25-name sample.

The exact metric/entity names are the terms to reuse in the follow-up call; `structuredContent.matches[].coverage.items[]` pairs each name with its `id`. Search on the EXACT name returned — `tako_search` matches the graph's own names and takes no pin. An `id` is for `tako_graph_related` traversal, not for the search call. When the measure is known, `next_call` is that follow-up prewritten — run it verbatim.

A broad entity's coverage list is capped and may be truncated: treat a name you don't see as UNCONFIRMED rather than absent. This tool confirms a name EXISTS in the graph; it cannot confirm a chart exists behind it — the `next_call` is that check, and if it comes back with 0 cards, report the gap rather than rephrasing: one retrieval on the canonical name is the best evidence available, not proof of absence. On the discovery path, `found: true` means a match has live coverage, never that a name merely resolved; on the lookup path it means the entity holds something matching, and `verified` says what was checked. `found: false` is a real answer: report the gap rather than silently falling back to web.

Parameters:
- `q` (string, required, min 2 chars): The NAME of the entity (or metric) to look up. Put the measure in `metric`, not here.
- `metric` (string, optional, min 2 chars): The measure you want, when you already know it — e.g. "gross margin", "capex". Supplying it selects the fast lookup path above.
- `types` (string, "entity" | "metric", optional): Narrow resolution to a thing ("entity") or a measure ("metric"); omit to search both.
- `label` (string, optional): NER label to prefer — a boost, not a filter. Supply it when you can categorize the term (company→ORG, country→GPE, person→PERSON, metric→METRIC, …). Describes the ENTITY only; it is not applied to `metric`.
- `limit` (integer, 1–20, optional, default 10): How many candidate nodes to resolve. Every candidate comes back with its node id, type, subtype, label, and aliases; only the top few are coverage-checked.

### tako_graph_related
Listed by default. Explore what a graph node connects to — the map of what data Tako has for it. Covers what `tako_available_data` does not: traversal relations (siblings, part_of, members, `rel:*` named edges like `rel:competes_with`), server-side `q` filtering within a relation, and cursor paging past the first page. The map (`node_id` alone) gives each relation group's `key`, `label`, `total`, and a preview of its first three NAMES — no ids. Drill (`relation: "<key>"`) pages one group; its items carry `id`, `name` and `kind`, and only the focal node carries aliases and a truncated description. `q` is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING match on names and aliases, one string per call. A listed metric is table-level evidence, not proof — `tako_search` is the final validator. Empty `items` is a normal answer: say Tako holds nothing there rather than silently falling back to web.

Parameters:
- `node_id` (string, required): Node id from `tako_available_data` or a card's `nodes`.
- `relation` (string, optional): Relation key to page — metrics, entities, siblings, part_of, members, or rel:<phrase>. Omit for the overview.
- `q` (string, optional): Case-insensitive substring filter on name+aliases — one string per call; for several name-variants of a metric ("revenue", "sales"), call once per variant.
- `label` (string, optional) / `infer_label` (boolean, optional): NER label to prefer when resolving — a boost, not a filter.
- `cursor` (string, optional) / `limit` (integer, 1-100, default 50): Pagination within a drilled relation.

### tako_visualize
Opt-in tool — name `visualize` in `?tools=` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Listed by default on the ChatGPT app surface (`/mcp/chatgpt`), which renders its chart inline as a widget; everywhere else enable it for the shareable embed URL. Create a Tako card from your OWN structured data (not from search), backed by Tako's Thin-Viz API. This is the one tool on the surface that WRITES, and what it writes is world-readable: the data you send is stored by Tako, the card does not expire, and anyone holding the returned url can open it without signing in. Confirm the user wants a public card before you call. Provide one or more typed components; the card auto-renders inline as a chart.

The result on `/mcp` is four fields on both channels — `title`, `url` (the card's page on Tako), `embed_url` (iframe) and `image_url` (PNG) — and the text channel renders the same four as `## Card created` plus a fact list, because many hosts feed the model only that channel. The chart-widget fields (`pub_id`, `dark_mode`, `width`, `height`) ship on `/mcp/chatgpt` alone, where the widget reads them. On `/mcp`, a client that declares MCP Apps support gets the chart as a live card in the widget, and any other client gets it as a PNG content block.

Parameters:
- `components` (array, required): One or more `{ component_type, config, component_variant? }` objects, rendered top to bottom. `component_type` is one of: header, generic_timeseries, categorical_bar, choropleth, data_table_chart, histogram, pie, table, financial_boxes, timeline, treemap, heatmap, marimekko, boxplot, waterfall, sankey, scatter, bubble, top_level_metric, person_card. `header`, `categorical_bar`, `generic_timeseries`, `table`, `financial_boxes` and `pie` carry their required fields inline in the published input schema; the rest take a passthrough config validated server-side. The optional `component_variant` string selects a type variant (e.g. 'simple', 'financial'). `person_card` must be the only component.
- `title` (string, optional): Card title. Omitted, a `header` component's title is used.
- `description` (string, optional): Card description, shown under the title. Not echoed back on the result.
- `source` (string, optional): Data source attribution shown in the card footer
- `height` (integer, 100-2000, optional): Card height in pixels
- `normalize_currencies` (string, optional): Target ISO 4217 code to convert currency-denominated datasets

Never send sensitive data in `components` — it becomes a public page. No credentials, payment or bank details, health information, government identifiers, precise home addresses, or personal data the subject has not agreed to publish.

### tako_agent
Opt-in tool — name `agent` in `?tools=` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Run Tako's Answer Agent only when the user asks for one: they name Tako's agent or ask for deep or multi-step research with Tako. Otherwise, use `tako_search`. Best for an ask for Tako's agent whose answer is a chart or a written finding; for a list of companies or people, use `tako_company_agent` instead. Returns a written `answer` with numbered citations plus the chart `cards` it built. Listed by default on the ChatGPT app surface (`/mcp/chatgpt`), where every card renders inline as a chart. A call returns within 45 s. If `status` is `running`, call again with `run_id`; don't start a new run.

Parameters:
- `query` (string, optional): The question to research, in natural language. Ask one question per call; the agent plans its own sub-steps. Send `query` or `run_id`, not both.
- `run_id` (string, optional): A `run_id` from an earlier call that returned `status: running`. Send it instead of `query` to keep waiting for that run.
- `sources` (array, optional): Which corpora to search; default is both (`["data","web"]`). Keep both unless the user asks for one.
- `thread_id` (string UUID, optional): A `thread_id` from an earlier run. Pass it back to ask a follow-up in that conversation; omit it to start a new one.

### tako_company_agent
Opt-in tool — name `company_agent` in `?tools=` on the endpoint URL (see Connecting). Run Tako's Company Agent only when the user asks for one: they name Tako's agent or ask for deep or multi-step research with Tako. Otherwise, use `tako_search`, even for a list that search can't fully filter. Best for an ask for Tako's Company Agent, or an ask for Tako's agent to build a list of companies or people: companies by location, industry, status, founding date, funding stage, or size, and the officers, directors, owners, or employees of those companies. It searches company registries, company and people profiles, and the web, and returns a written `answer` with numbered citations plus the list `cards` it built. Listed by default on the ChatGPT app surface (`/mcp/chatgpt`), where every card renders inline. A call returns within 45 s. If `status` is `running`, call again with `run_id`; don't start a new run.

Parameters:
- `query` (string, optional): The question to research, in natural language. Ask one question per call. Send `query` or `run_id`, not both.
- `run_id` (string, optional): A `company_run_` `run_id` from an earlier call that returned `status: running`. Send it instead of `query` to keep waiting for that run.
- `sources` (array, optional): Which corpora to search; default is both (`["data","web"]`).
- `thread_id` (string UUID, optional): A `thread_id` from an earlier run. Pass it back to ask a follow-up in that conversation; omit it to start a new one.
- `effort` (string, optional): Research depth. `medium` is the default; `high` is stronger and slower. `low` can't filter or rank by financial metrics such as revenue or headcount. Effort is fixed for a thread.
